new_statements.translation: In polysyllabic non-compound words the strongest pressure [= stress] falls on the stem syllable, with a single exception, such as […] (leeuwerik 'lark'). Among the compounds the following deserve attention: […] (aalbessen 'currants'), […] (bijkans 'almost'), […] (giertij 'spring tide'), […] (hoogdag, i.e. Christmas, Easter and Whitsun), […] (roodvonk 'scarlet fever'; […]), […] (somtijds 'sometimes'), […] (zoethout 'liquorice'), […] (zoutevisch 'salt fish'). […] Foreign words have been taken over with their own stress: […] (opril, Fr. appareil; […]), […] (hoefstal 'shoeing frame', cf. Fr. travail), […] (Fr. visite); except […] ('tea pail'; Fr. guéridon). Syncope of ə in words such as […] (direct), […] (gelijk 'alike'), […] (gareel 'harness'), […] (kalander) points to particularly strong pressure in the stressed syllable. [The bracketed items are Verschuur's phonetic transcriptions, omitted here; in the listed compounds his stress mark stands after the final element.]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Main stress falls on the stem (root) syllable of the word; in native non-compound words this is the first syllable of the stem (unstressed prefixes such as be-, ver-, ge- reduce to schwa, cf. Van Weel 1904 §109 and Landheer 1955 §32). Loanwords keep the stress of the source language (often non-initial), and a set of compounds carry the stress on their final element. Landheer 1955: 142 (Overflakkee) states that main stress corresponds to that of Standard Dutch and marks the stressed syllable by number in his vocabulary, chiefly for loanwords.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Verschuur 1902 says nothing about secondary stress. Landheer 1955 §§34-35, pp. 37-38 (Overflakkee): the first syllable of longer loanwords carries 'een vrij krachtige bijtoon' and its vowel weakens but does not become schwa; suffixes with secondary stress (-ien, -baer, -saem, -lei, -ie, -heit, -dom, -ier, -loos) and the prefixes of-, an-, bie- (when stressed) keep their full vowel.
new_statements.exceptions: Verschuur: leeuwerik 'lark' (stress not on the stem syllable); compounds with the stress on the final element (aalbessen, bijkans, giertij, hoogdag, roodvonk, somtijds, zoethout, zoutevisch); loanwords keep foreign (usually final) stress, except guéridon > 'thee-emmer' which was nativized. Van Weel 1904 §109: jiffrouwe 'juffrouw' keeps a weakened accent on the initial syllable; plural pronouns wulder/julder/hulder show stress retraction. Landheer 1955 §33: loanword types with schwa in the first syllable (fesoen, ketoor, meziek, erloozje, kendiesie, etc.).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: isolated words ('afzonderlijke woorden'); Verschuur explicitly did not study the musical sentence accent (§2, p. 2) and treats exclamatory sentence stress separately (§3). Describes the dialect of Noord-Beveland; corroborated for Overflakkee by Landheer 1955 (main stress = Standard Dutch).
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding statement (Verschuur 1902) describes the dialect of Noord-Beveland (Noord-Bevelands), a Midden-Zeeuws subdialect of Zeeuws; Landheer 1955 describes Overflakkee (Flakkees, Goeree-Overflakkee, province of Zuid-Holland but conventionally grouped with Zeeuws) and Van Weel 1904 West-Voorne (Goeree); De Vin 1952 Schouwen-Duiveland. Glottolog 5.1 lists no separate dialect glottocodes for these under zeeu1238 in the target record. Two Glottolog 'phonology' items (Versieck 1989 Maldegem, Taeldeman 1966 Kleit) concern East-Flanders localities and are probably misfiled under Zeeuws.

sources.note: §3 'dynamiek', pp. 3-4: in polysyllabic non-compound words the strongest pressure (stress) falls on the stem syllable, one exception noted (leeuwerik 'lark'); a list of compounds 'deserving attention' whose transcriptions carry the stress mark on the final element (aalbessen, bijkans, giertij, hoogdag, roodvonk, somtijds, zoethout, zoutevisch); foreign words are taken over with their own stress (opril, hoefstal, visite; except guéridon 'thee-emmer'); syncope of schwa points to very strong stress in the stressed syllable. Musical sentence accent not investigated (§2).

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Klankleer ch. I (pp. 1-26) has a section 'Opmerkingen over klankkarakter, articulatie, spreektempo en kwantiteit' (pp. 2-5) but no general statement on word stress; incidental remarks only: baajeneer 'baanderheer' 'met klemtoon op de laatste lettergreep', treated as a loan from Standard Dutch (p. 27); demonstrative die 'heeft altijd zware klemtoon' (p. 40); allegro forms shortened 'door hun klemtoon' (p. 3).
Section 'Het accent' is about pronunciation style, nothing about word stress.
